title: Verifying a Rational Trigonometric Identity
originalTopic: Trigonometric Identities: Common Denominators and Pythagorean Reductions
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Verify the trigonometric identity by simplifying the left-hand side: cos(x)/(1 - sin(x)) - cos(x)/(1 + sin(x)) = 2*tan(x).

steps.title: Combine Fractions over a Common Denominator
steps.mathExpression: \frac{\cos x(1 + \sin x) - \cos x(1 - \sin x)}{(1 - \sin x)(1 + \sin x)}
steps.explanation: Find a common denominator by multiplying the conjugate binomial denominators (1 - sin x)(1 + sin x).
steps.why: Standard algebraic fraction subtraction requires a common denominator.

steps.title: Expand and Simplify Numerator and Denominator
steps.mathExpression: \frac{\cos x + \cos x\sin x - \cos x + \cos x\sin x}{1 - \sin^2 x} = \frac{2\cos x\sin x}{1 - \sin^2 x}
steps.explanation: The linear terms cos(x) cancel in the numerator, combining the cross-terms into 2*cos(x)*sin(x). The denominator forms a difference of squares 1 - sin^2(x).
steps.why: Expansion of conjugate products produces difference of squares (1 - sin^2 x).

steps.title: Apply Pythagorean Identity and Reduce
steps.mathExpression: \frac{2\cos x\sin x}{\cos^2 x} = 2\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = 2\tan x
steps.explanation: Substitute the Pythagorean identity 1 - sin^2(x) = cos^2(x) into the denominator and cancel one power of cos(x). The quotient sin(x)/cos(x) evaluates to tan(x).
steps.why: Pythagorean identity 1 - sin^2(x) = cos^2(x) and definition of tangent as sin/cos.
